description: Canonical M0 baseline: 1D selective near-zone recycle and respray with fixed throw distributions. Toy model; parameters are not real-world optima.

metric.primary: U(t) = sum_{i=1}^{K} (p_i(t) - 1/K)^2  (histogram squared-L2 distance to the uniform bin vector; MSE reading is U/K)
metric.secondary: TV(t) = 0.5 * sum_{i=1}^{K} |p_i(t) - 1/K|  (total variation distance; sanity check only)

experiments.question: Does the near-biased initial state produce a finite-time interior minimum (t_best > 0) after which continued operation worsens uniformity?
Negative control: is t = 0 already optimal, and does continued selective recycling only degrade uniformity?
Boundary control: does the improvement pattern of EXP-M0-A vanish or change when the initial bias direction mismatches the recycle action?
